steps.stem: A, B and C lie on a circle with center O, with B on the minor arc AC. Given: angle AOC is 112°. What is angle ABC?
explanation: B is on the minor arc AC. Stand at B between BA and BC: you see the major arc AC. Angle ABC rests on it.
The central angle on the major arc: \(360°-112°=248°\).
The inscribed angle is half of it: \(\angle ABC=\frac{248°}{2}=124°\).

Check: a point D on the major arc makes ABCD an inscribed quadrilateral. \(\angle ADC=\frac{112°}{2}=56°\), and \(\angle ABC=180°-56°=124°\). (\(180°-112°=68°\) is the trap: AOCB is not an inscribed quadrilateral.)

steps.stem: Chord AB of a circle with center O is 16 cm long. The distance from O to AB is 6 cm. What is the circumference of the circle (in cm)?
explanation: Draw the perpendicular OM from O to AB. It cuts the chord in half: \(AM=MB=\frac{16}{2}=8\).
Right triangle OMB: \(OB^2=6^2+8^2=100\), so the radius is \(OB=10\).
Circumference: \(2\pi\cdot10=20\pi\). (\(100\pi\) is the area, and \(10\pi\) takes 10 as the diameter.)

steps.stem: PD and PE are tangent to the circle at D and E. A lies on the major arc DE. Given: angle DPE is 52°. What is angle DAE?
explanation: Draw the radii OD and OE. A radius to a point of tangency is perpendicular to the tangent: \(\angle ODP=\angle OEP=90°\).
The angles of quadrilateral ODPE add up to \(360°\): \(\angle DOE=360°-90°-90°-52°=128°\).
Angle DAE is an inscribed angle on the same minor arc DE: \(\angle DAE=\frac{128°}{2}=64°\).

steps.stem: A circle is inscribed in a right triangle whose legs are 8 cm and 15 cm. What is the radius of the circle (in cm)?
explanation: Hypotenuse: \(\sqrt{8^2+15^2}=\sqrt{289}=17\).
Tangent pieces from one vertex are equal. At the right angle both pieces are r, so the pieces on the hypotenuse are \(8-r\) and \(15-r\): \((8-r)+(15-r)=17\), so \(23-2r=17\) and \(r=3\).
Shortcut for a right triangle: \(r=\frac{a+b-c}{2}=\frac{8+15-17}{2}=3\). (\(8.5\) is half the hypotenuse: the radius of the circle around the triangle.)

steps.title: Circles — angle and tangent rules
steps.intro: One main rule — an inscribed angle is half the central angle on the same arc — and the rest follows.

head: Rule
What it says
rows: central \(=2\times\) inscribed, when both rest on the same arc
inscribed angles on the same arc (or on equal arcs) are equal
all 4 vertices on the circle \(\rightarrow\) opposite angles add up to \(180°\)
radius to the point of tangency \(\perp\) tangent — always draw that radius
equal lengths — with the two radii they make a kite
equal central angles and equal arcs (and back)
rests on a diameter: a right triangle's hypotenuse (a rectangle's diagonal) is a diameter
the perpendicular from the center cuts a chord in half: \(d^2+\left(\frac{\text{chord}}{2}\right)^2=r^2\)
tangent pieces from each vertex are equal; right triangle: \(r=\frac{a+b-c}{2}\)
distance between the centers: \(R+r\) (from outside) or \(R-r\) (from inside)

tips: Which arc? Stand at the vertex between the two "walls" — the arc you can see is the one the angle rests on.
A vertex at the centre O is not on the circle — a quadrilateral through O is not inscribed.
A central angle can be bigger than \(180°\) — it still counts.
Distance from the center to a chord? Draw the perpendicular — it halves the chord.

steps.stem: The numerical value of a circle’s area in cm² is 3 times as much as the numerical value of its circumference in cm. What is its radius (in cm)?
explanation: Area \(=3\times\) circumference: \(\pi r^2=3\cdot2\pi r\).
Divide by \(\pi\): \(r^2=6r\). Divide by \(r\) (a radius is not 0): \(r=6\).
Check: \(S=\pi\cdot6^2=36\pi\) and \(C=2\pi\cdot6=12\pi\), and \(36\pi=3\cdot12\pi\).

steps.stem: The circumference of a circle increases by 50%. By what percent does its area increase?
explanation: The circumference grows like the radius: the radius is multiplied by 1.5.
The area grows like the radius squared: \(1.5^2=2.25\).
The new area is \(225\%\) of the old one: an increase of \(225\%-100\%=125\%\).
Check with numbers: \(r=2\to3\). The area goes from \(4\pi\) to \(9\pi\): up \(5\pi\), and \(\frac{5\pi}{4\pi}=1.25=125\%\).

steps.stem: A circle with center O has radius 6 cm. The highlighted arc AB has length \(3\pi\) cm. What is α?
explanation: The whole circumference: \(2\pi\cdot6=12\pi\).
The arc is \(\frac{3\pi}{12\pi}=\frac14\) of the circle.
So its central angle is \(\frac14\) of \(360°\): \(\alpha=90°\).

steps.stem: A circle with center O has radius 6 cm. Two non-overlapping shaded sectors have central angles of 60° and 90°. What is their total area (in cm²)?
explanation: \(60°\) is \(\frac16\) of the circle and \(90°\) is \(\frac14\): \(\frac16+\frac14=\frac2{12}+\frac3{12}=\frac5{12}\).
The area of the circle: \(\pi\cdot6^2=36\pi\).
Shaded: \(\frac5{12}\cdot36\pi=15\pi\). (Or separately: \(6\pi+9\pi=15\pi\).)

steps.intro: Find the radius first; for sectors and arcs, find the fraction of the circle.

head: What
Formula
Remember
rows: the arc alone has no straight edges

tips: \(\pi\) is a number — a bit more than 3 (\(\approx3.14\)), not an unknown. Keep it in the answer.
Given \(C\) or \(S\)? Go back to \(r\) first, then on to the other one.
Radius from an area: take the positive root.
A regular hexagon in a circle: its side equals the radius (six equilateral triangles).

steps.stem: AB is a diameter of a circle with center O, and \(AB=12\) cm. Given: angle AOC is 120°. What is the area of the shaded triangle OBC (in cm²)?
explanation: AB is a straight line: \(\angle BOC=180°-120°=60°\).
\(OB=OC\) (radii), so the base angles are equal: \(\frac{180°-60°}{2}=60°\) each. Triangle OBC is equilateral.
Its side is a radius: \(\frac{12}{2}=6\).
Area of an equilateral triangle: \(\frac{6^2\sqrt3}{4}=\frac{36\sqrt3}{4}=9\sqrt3\).

steps.stem: An isosceles triangle ABC is inscribed in a circle with center O, with \(AB=AC\). Given: angle BAC is 40°. What is angle ABO?
explanation: The central angle on arc BC: \(\angle BOC=2\cdot40°=80°\).
Triangle BOC is isosceles (\(OB=OC\)): \(\angle OBC=\frac{180°-80°}{2}=50°\).
Triangle ABC is isosceles (\(AB=AC\)): \(\angle ABC=\frac{180°-40°}{2}=70°\).
Faster: the radius OA splits angle A in half, \(\frac{40°}{2}=20°\). Triangle AOB is isosceles (\(OA=OB\)), so \(\angle ABO=\angle BAO=20°\).

AE is a diameter of a circle with center O. B, C and D lie on the same semicircle, in that order. Given:
\(\begin{cases} AB=BC=CD=DE \\ AO=3\text{ cm} \end{cases}\)
Which of the following statements is not true?
explanation: Angles DAE and CAD are inscribed angles on the equal chords DE and CD, so they are equal. Statement 1 is true.
The four equal chords cut off four equal central angles. Together they make the straight angle AOE: \(4x=180°\), so \(x=45°\). Statement 2 is true.
Angle ADE is an inscribed angle on the diameter AE: \(90°\). Statement 3 is true.
Triangle AOC: \(AO=OC=3\) and \(\angle AOC=45°+45°=90°\). A 45°-45°-90° triangle: \(AC=3\sqrt2\neq3\sqrt3\). Statement 4 is not true.

steps.stem: Two congruent circles with centers O and M are externally tangent. Each has radius 4 cm. MA and MB are tangent to the circle with center O at A and B. What is the smaller angle AOB?
explanation: Radius to the point of tangency: \(OA\perp MA\) and \(OB\perp MB\).
The circles are tangent, so the distance between the centers is the sum of the radii: \(OM=4+4=8\).
Right triangle OAM: the leg \(OA=4\) is half of the hypotenuse \(OM=8\). It is a 30°-60°-90° triangle: \(\angle AMO=30°\) and \(\angle AOM=60°\).
By symmetry, \(\angle BOM=60°\) too: \(\angle AOB=60°+60°=120°\).

steps.stem: The circumference of the smaller circle is \(8\pi\) cm, and the shaded area inside the larger circle but outside the smaller one is \(65\pi\) cm². Between which two values is the circumference of the larger circle (in cm)?
explanation: Small circle: \(2\pi r=8\pi\), so \(r=4\). Its area: \(\pi\cdot4^2=16\pi\).
Large circle: \(16\pi+65\pi=81\pi\), so \(R^2=81\) and \(R=9\).
Circumference: \(2\pi\cdot9=18\pi\approx18\cdot3.14=56.52\) — between 56 and 57.

explanation: \(7^2+24^2=49+576=625=25^2\), so the triangle is a right triangle. The right angle is opposite the side 25.
An inscribed right angle rests on a diameter. So the hypotenuse is a diameter of the circle: \(d=25\).

explanation: The twelve angles make a full turn: \(6\alpha+6\beta=360°\), so \(\alpha+\beta=60°\).
The two shaded sectors are \(\frac{60°}{360°}=\frac16\) of the circle.
The area of the circle: \(\pi(\sqrt{30})^2=30\pi\). Shaded: \(\frac16\cdot30\pi=5\pi\).

explanation: For tangent circles, the distance between the centers is the sum of the radii: \(AB=2+4=6\), \(AC=2+6=8\) and \(BC=4+6=10\).
The arc inside that angle is \(\frac14\) of circle A. The highlighted arc is the other \(\frac34\).
Circumference of circle A: \(2\pi\cdot2=4\pi\). Highlighted arc: \(\frac34\cdot4\pi=3\pi\).

explanation: The wire becomes the whole circumference: \(2\pi r=10\).
\(r=\frac{10}{2\pi}=\frac5\pi\).

explanation: Small circle: \(\pi d=6\pi\), so its diameter OB is 6.
OB is a radius of the large circle: \(R=6\).
Large circumference: \(2\pi\cdot6=12\pi\).

explanation: The large radius is 6, and the small radius is \(\frac62=3\).
Areas: \(\pi\cdot6^2=36\pi\) and \(\pi\cdot3^2=9\pi\).

steps.stem: Two concentric circles have radii 2 cm and 3 cm. What is the ratio of the area between the circles to the area of the smaller disk?
explanation: The area between the circles: \(\pi\cdot3^2-\pi\cdot2^2=9\pi-4\pi=5\pi\).
The smaller disk: \(\pi\cdot2^2=4\pi\).
The ratio: \(5\pi:4\pi=5:4\).

steps.stem: A machine paints 600 m² per hour on a smooth surface. On a rough surface its rate is halved. How many hours does it need to paint a rough circular floor of radius 15 meters?
explanation: On the rough surface the rate is \(600\div2=300\) m² per hour.
The floor area is \(\pi\cdot15^2=225\pi\) m². Time \(=\) work \(\div\) rate \(=\frac{225\pi}{300}=\frac{3\pi}{4}\) hours.

steps.stem: The area of a circle is multiplied by 9. By what number is its circumference multiplied?
explanation: Area \(\times9=\times3^2\), so the radius is multiplied by 3.
The circumference grows like the radius: \(\times3\).
Check: \(r=1\to3\). \(C=2\pi\to6\pi\) (\(\times3\)) and \(S=\pi\to9\pi\) (\(\times9\)).

steps.stem: The radius of a circle is increased by 20%. By what percent does its area increase?
explanation: The new radius is \(1.2r\). Area: \(\pi(1.2r)^2=1.44\pi r^2\).
The area is multiplied by 1.44: an increase of \(44\%\) (not \(20\%\) — area grows like \(r^2\)).

steps.stem: AB and CD are diameters of a circle with center O. Given: angle COB is \(5\alpha\), angle BOD is \(\alpha\), and angle DOA is \(\beta\). What is \(\beta\)?
explanation: COB and BOD make the straight angle COD: \(5\alpha+\alpha=180°\), so \(\alpha=30°\).
BOD and DOA make the straight angle BOA: \(30°+\beta=180°\), so \(\beta=150°\).

explanation: On the same arc, the central angle is twice the inscribed angle: \(\alpha=2\beta\).
\(3\beta-\alpha=3\beta-2\beta=\beta\).

steps.stem: Two opposite angles of a quadrilateral inscribed in a circle are \(3x\) degrees and \((2x+20)\) degrees. What is x?
explanation: Opposite angles of an inscribed quadrilateral add up to \(180°\): \(3x+(2x+20)=180\).

steps.stem: Triangle ABC is inscribed in a circle, and angle BAC is 36°. What fraction of the circumference is the major arc BC, which contains A?
explanation: The minor arc BC has the central angle \(2\cdot36°=72°\). That is \(\frac{72}{360}=\frac15\) of the circle.
The major arc BC is the rest: \(1-\frac15=\frac45\).

steps.stem: Two runners leave the same point on a circular track at the same time, in opposite directions. One runs five times as fast as the other. At their first meeting, what central angle corresponds to the arc traveled by the slower runner?
explanation: At their first meeting, together they have covered one full circle.
Equal times: their distances are in the same ratio as their speeds, \(1:5\). The circle is \(1+5=6\) parts, and the slower runner covers \(1\) part: \(\frac16\) of the circle.
Central angle: \(\frac{360°}{6}=60°\).

steps.stem: A sector has radius 10 cm and central angle 72°. What is its perimeter (in cm)?
explanation: \(72°\) is \(\frac15\) of the circle. Circumference: \(2\pi\cdot10=20\pi\), so the arc is \(\frac15\cdot20\pi=4\pi\).
Perimeter of the sector: arc \(+\) two radii \(=4\pi+20\).

steps.stem: A circle with center O has radius 8 cm. Three radii divide it into sectors of 135°, 90°, and a third angle. What is the length of the arc belonging to the third sector (in cm)?
explanation: The third angle: \(360°-135°-90°=135°\). That is \(\frac{135}{360}=\frac38\) of the circle.
Circumference: \(2\pi\cdot8=16\pi\). Arc: \(\frac38\cdot16\pi=6\pi\).

explanation: \(\angle COB=180°-36°=144°\). That is \(\frac{144}{360}=\frac25\) of the circle.
Sector: \(\frac25\cdot25\pi=10\pi\).

steps.stem: AD and BC are diameters of two externally tangent circles. ABCD is a square with perimeter 28 cm. What is the sum of the circumferences of the circles (in cm)?
explanation: Side of the square: \(\frac{28}{4}=7\). AD and BC are sides, so each diameter is 7.
Each circumference: \(\pi\cdot7=7\pi\). Sum: \(7\pi+7\pi=14\pi\).

explanation: OT is a radius to the point of tangency: \(OT\perp AB\). So OT is the height of triangle AOB: 5.

PT is tangent at T to a circle with center O. Given:
\(\begin{cases} OP=17\text{ cm} \\ OT=8\text{ cm} \end{cases}\)
What is PT (in cm)?
explanation: \(OT\perp PT\) (radius to the point of tangency), so triangle OTP is a right triangle with hypotenuse OP.

steps.stem: PA and PB are tangent segments from P to a circle with center O. Given: \(PA=12\) cm and the circle radius is 5 cm. What is OP (in cm)?
explanation: \(OA\perp PA\) (radius to the point of tangency).

steps.stem: A circle with center B and radius 4 cm lies inside a circle with center A and radius 9 cm. The two circles touch at one point. What is AB (in cm)?
explanation: One circle inside the other, touching: the distance between the centers is the difference of the radii.
\(AB=9-4=5\). (13 is the distance for circles that touch from outside.)

steps.stem: A chord is 5 cm from the center of a circle with radius 13 cm. What is the length of the chord (in cm)?
explanation: The perpendicular from the center to a chord cuts it in half.
Right triangle: radius 13 (hypotenuse), distance 5, half chord: \(\sqrt{13^2-5^2}=\sqrt{144}=12\).
The chord: \(2\cdot12=24\).

explanation: \(\pi r^2=16\pi\), so \(r=4\) and the diameter is 8.
No chord is longer than the diameter. A chord of length 8 is a diameter: AC is a diameter.
An inscribed angle on a diameter is \(90°\): \(\angle ABC=90°\).

steps.stem: Which of the following figures cannot be inscribed in a circle?
choices: A kite whose two unequal opposite angles are 90° and 72°
An isosceles trapezoid with upper base angles of 104°
A rectangle with sides 3 cm and 40 cm
explanation: A quadrilateral can be inscribed in a circle only if its opposite angles add up to \(180°\).
The kite: \(90°+72°=162°\neq180°\). It cannot be inscribed.
The trapezoid (\(104°+76°=180°\)), the rectangle and a regular polygon can all be inscribed.

steps.stem: Quadrilateral ABCD is inscribed in a circle of area \(25\pi\) cm². Diagonal AC bisects both angle A and angle C. What is AC (in cm)?
explanation: Write the angles at A and C as \(2\alpha\) and \(2\beta\). Opposite angles of an inscribed quadrilateral: \(2\alpha+2\beta=180°\), so \(\alpha+\beta=90°\).
In triangle ABC: \(\angle B=180°-\alpha-\beta=90°\). An inscribed right angle rests on a diameter: AC is a diameter.

steps.stem: AB is tangent to a circle with center O and radius 4 cm. Given: \(OA=OB\) and angle AOB is 90°. What is the area inside triangle AOB but outside the circle (in cm²)?
explanation: Draw the radius OC to the point of tangency: \(OC\perp AB\) and \(OC=4\).
Triangle AOB is right and isosceles, so its height OC is also a median. Triangles AOC and BOC are 45°-45°-90° triangles: \(AC=CB=OC=4\), and \(AB=8\).
Triangle: \(\frac{8\cdot4}{2}=16\). Sector (\(90°\) is a quarter): \(\frac14\cdot\pi\cdot4^2=4\pi\).
Shaded: \(16-4\pi\).

steps.stem: ABC is a right triangle whose sides AB and AC are tangent to a circle with center O at B and D, respectively. B, O, E and C lie on one straight line, and E is on the circle. Given: \(OE=EC=12\) cm. What is the area of the shaded region between CD, CE and the minor arc DE (in cm²)?
explanation: OE is a radius: \(OD=OE=12\), and \(OC=12+12=24\).
Draw the radius OD to the point of tangency: \(OD\perp AC\), so triangle ODC is a right triangle.
The hypotenuse OC is twice the leg OD: a 30°-60°-90° triangle. \(\angle DOC=60°\) and \(DC=12\sqrt3\).
Triangle ODC: \(\frac{12\cdot12\sqrt3}{2}=72\sqrt3\). Sector DOE (\(60°\) is a sixth): \(\frac16\cdot\pi\cdot12^2=24\pi\).
Shaded: \(72\sqrt3-24\pi\).

steps.stem: A semicircle has center O and radius r. A and B lie on its curved boundary, and angle OAB is 60°. What is the ratio of the perimeter of the semicircle to the perimeter of triangle AOB?
explanation: \(OA=OB=r\), so the base angles of triangle AOB are equal: both are \(60°\). The triangle is equilateral, and its perimeter is \(3r\).
The perimeter of the semicircle is half the circumference plus the diameter: \(\pi r+2r=(\pi+2)r\).
Ratio: \(\frac{(\pi+2)r}{3r}=\frac{\pi+2}{3}\).
Check with \(r=2\): \(\frac{2\pi+4}{6}=\frac{\pi+2}{3}\). A ratio of two perimeters cannot contain r.

explanation: Let the radius be r. The side of ABCD is a diameter, \(2r\), so its area is \((2r)^2=4r^2\).
The diagonal of EFGH is a diameter, \(2r\). Area of a square from its diagonal: \(\frac{(2r)^2}{2}=2r^2\).

steps.title: Shapes inside circles — know them by heart
steps.intro: Three nested objects that show up on the exam, and the ratio rule behind all of them.
tips: A square inside a circle: its diagonal is a diameter. A square around a circle: its side is a diameter.
Perimeter ÷ perimeter or area ÷ area: the radius must cancel — an answer with \(r\) is a distractor.
Plug in \(r=1\) — but if answers multiply or divide by \(r\), use \(r=2\).
Tangent point? Draw the radius to it — it makes a right angle.

steps.stem:
A circle with center O has radius 9 cm. A, G, F, E and D lie on the same arc, in that order. B and C lie on the arc AD that does not contain F. Given:
\(\begin{cases} \angle ABF=26° \\ \angle FCD=49° \\ \angle GOE=90° \end{cases}\)
What is the sum of the lengths of the highlighted arcs AG and ED (in cm)?
explanation: Angle ABF is an inscribed angle on arc AF. The central angle is twice as big: \(\angle AOF=2\cdot26°=52°\).
Angle FCD is an inscribed angle on arc FD: \(\angle FOD=2\cdot49°=98°\).
\(\angle AOD=52°+98°=150°\). Take away the middle part: \(\angle AOG+\angle EOD=150°-90°=60°\).
The two arcs together are \(\frac{60°}{360°}=\frac16\) of the circumference \(2\pi\cdot9=18\pi\): \(\frac16\cdot18\pi=3\pi\).

steps.stem: Two congruent circles with centers O and P have radius 4 cm and intersect at A and B. The minor arc AB is one quarter of the circumference of each circle. What is the area of the union of the two disks (in cm²)?
explanation: A minor arc that is a quarter of the circle has a central angle of \(90°\): \(\angle AOB=\angle APB=90°\).
\(OA=AP=PB=BO=4\), and the angles are \(90°\): OAPB is a square with area \(4^2=16\).
Outside the square, each disk leaves a sector of \(360°-90°=270°\), which is \(\frac34\) of the disk: \(\frac34\cdot\pi\cdot4^2=12\pi\).

steps.stem: A circle with center O has radius 3 cm. The opposite sides AD and BC of rectangle ABCD are tangent to the circle at E and F, respectively. The area of the rectangle equals the area of the circle. What is the length of BC (in cm)?
explanation: The tangents AD and BC are parallel, so the distance between them is a diameter: \(AB=2\cdot3=6\).
The area of the circle: \(\pi\cdot3^2=9\pi\).
\(6\cdot BC=9\pi\), so \(BC=\frac{9\pi}{6}=\frac{3\pi}{2}\).
Size check: the circle is smaller than the square around it (\(6\cdot6=36\)). So \(6\cdot BC<36\) and \(BC<6\). Only \(\frac{3\pi}{2}\approx4.7\) fits.

steps.stem: A smaller circle lies inside a larger circle and is internally tangent to it at A. AB is a diameter of the larger circle, AC is a diameter of the smaller circle, and \(CB=6\) cm. The area inside the larger circle but outside the smaller one is \(21\pi\) cm². What is the radius of the smaller circle (in cm)?
explanation: Let the small radius be r. Then \(AC=2r\), and the large diameter is \(AB=2r+6\). So \(R=\frac{2r+6}{2}=r+3\).
Shaded: \(\pi(r+3)^2-\pi r^2=21\pi\).
Divide by \(\pi\) and expand: \(r^2+6r+9-r^2=21\), so \(6r+9=21\) and \(r=2\).

ABC is an isosceles triangle. Given:
\(\begin{cases} AB=AC \\ \angle BAC=2\alpha\text{ degrees, where }0<\alpha<90 \end{cases}\)
B lies on a circle with center O and radius r. AB and BC meet the circle again at D and E, respectively. What is the length of the arc DE that does not contain B?
explanation: The base angles are equal: \(\angle ABC=\frac{180°-2\alpha}{2}=90°-\alpha\).
Angle DBE is the same angle, and it is an inscribed angle on arc DE. The central angle is twice as big: \(180°-2\alpha\).
Arc: \(\frac{180-2\alpha}{360}\cdot2\pi r=\frac{180-2\alpha}{180}\cdot\pi r=\pi r\left(1-\frac{\alpha}{90}\right)\).
Check with \(\alpha=30\) and \(r=1\): the central angle is \(120°\), and the arc is \(\frac13\cdot2\pi=\frac{2\pi}{3}\). Only \(\pi\left(1-\frac{30}{90}\right)=\frac{2\pi}{3}\) fits.

steps.stem: In a circle with center O and radius 6 cm, angle AOB is 60°. What is the area of the shaded region between chord AB and arc AB (in cm²)?
explanation: Segment \(=\) sector \(-\) triangle.
Sector: \(60°\) is \(\frac16\) of the circle: \(\frac16\cdot\pi\cdot6^2=6\pi\).
Triangle AOB: \(OA=OB=6\) and \(\angle AOB=60°\), so it is equilateral with side 6: \(\frac{6^2\sqrt3}{4}=9\sqrt3\).
Segment: \(6\pi-9\sqrt3\). (\(3\pi-9\sqrt3\) is negative: \(3\pi\approx9.4\) and \(9\sqrt3\approx15.6\).)

steps.stem: Two circles with centers A and B touch each other from the outside. Their radii are 8 cm and 2 cm. A line touches the two circles at D and C, as in the figure. What is the length of DC (in cm)?
explanation: Draw the radii AD and BC. Both are perpendicular to the line DC, so ABCD is a right trapezoid. The centers: \(AB=8+2=10\).
Draw BE parallel to DC, with E on AD: \(AE=8-2=6\) and \(BE=DC\).
Right triangle ABE: \(DC=BE=\sqrt{10^2-6^2}=\sqrt{64}=8\).
Shortcut for circles that touch: \(DC=2\sqrt{Rr}=2\sqrt{8\cdot2}=8\).

steps.stem: Four equal arcs of a circle have a combined length equal to \(\frac25\) of its circumference. What is the central angle subtending one of these arcs?
explanation: The four equal arcs are \(\frac25\) of the circle, so one arc is \(\frac25\div4=\frac1{10}\) of the circle.
Its central angle: \(\frac1{10}\cdot360°=36°\).

steps.stem: Four semicircular arcs have radii whose average is m. What is the sum of the lengths of the four curved arcs?
explanation: A semicircular arc with radius r has length \(\frac{2\pi r}{2}=\pi r\).
The four radii add up to \(4m\) (their average is m). So the four arcs add up to \(\pi\cdot4m=4\pi m\).

steps.stem: A sector has central angle 150°. Its area, measured in cm², is numerically 3 times as much as its arc length, measured in cm. What is the radius of its circle (in cm)?
explanation: Let f be the fraction of the circle: \(f=\frac{150}{360}\).
Sector area \(=f\cdot\pi r^2\) and arc \(=f\cdot2\pi r\): \(f\pi r^2=3\cdot f\cdot2\pi r\).
Divide by \(f\pi r\): \(r=6\). (The angle does not matter.)

steps.stem: A wheel of radius 12 cm rolls without slipping along a straight path of length \(3.6\pi\) m. How many complete revolutions does it make?
explanation: Same units first: \(3.6\pi\) m \(=360\pi\) cm.
One turn covers one circumference: \(2\pi\cdot12=24\pi\) cm.

steps.stem: A circular garden has radius 600 m. A path 100 m wide is built around its entire outside edge. What is the area of the path (in km²)?
explanation: Same units first: the inner radius is \(600\) m \(=0.6\) km, and the outer radius is \(600+100=700\) m \(=0.7\) km.
Path \(=\) big disk \(-\) small disk: \(\pi\cdot0.7^2-\pi\cdot0.6^2=\pi(0.49-0.36)=0.13\pi\) km².

steps.stem: AD is a diameter. B, C, F and G divide one semicircular arc AD into five equal arcs, and E is the midpoint of arc AB. What is angle ADE?
explanation: Five equal arcs on a semicircle: \(\frac{180°}{5}=36°\) each.
E is the midpoint of arc AB, so arc AE is \(\frac{36°}{2}=18°\).
Angle ADE is an inscribed angle on arc AE: \(\frac{18°}{2}=9°\).

steps.stem: AB is a diameter of a circle with radius 5 cm. C lies on one semicircular arc AB. Arc CB is twice as long as arc AC. What is BC (in cm)?
explanation: Arc CB is twice arc AC, and together they make the semicircle: arc AC \(=60°\) and arc CB \(=120°\).
Inscribed angles: \(\angle ABC=30°\), \(\angle BAC=60°\), and \(\angle ACB=90°\) (on the diameter).
A 30°-60°-90° triangle with hypotenuse \(AB=10\): \(AC=5\) and \(BC=5\sqrt3\).

explanation: OC is a radius (6), and it is also the diagonal of the square OACD.
Side of a square from its diagonal: \(OA=\frac{6}{\sqrt2}=3\sqrt2\).
\(OB=6\), so \(AB=OB-OA=6-3\sqrt2\).

explanation: Square: \(6^2=36\). Semicircle with radius 3: \(\frac{\pi\cdot3^2}{2}=\frac{9\pi}{2}=4.5\pi\).

explanation: The three sector angles are the angles of the triangle: together \(180°\).
With the same radius 3, the three sectors make half a disk: \(\frac12\cdot\pi\cdot3^2=\frac{9\pi}{2}\).

steps.stem: A rectangle with sides 10 cm and 24 cm is inscribed in a circle. What is the area of the circle (in cm²)?
explanation: Each angle of the rectangle is \(90°\), so its diagonal is a diameter of the circle around it.
Area: \(\pi\cdot13^2=169\pi\).

steps.stem: A circle is inscribed in a right triangle whose legs are 6 cm and 8 cm. What is the circle’s radius (in cm)?
explanation: Hypotenuse: \(\sqrt{6^2+8^2}=10\).
Tangent pieces from one vertex are equal. At the right angle both pieces are r, so the pieces on the hypotenuse are \(6-r\) and \(8-r\): \((6-r)+(8-r)=10\), and \(r=2\).
Shortcut for a right triangle: \(r=\frac{a+b-c}{2}=\frac{6+8-10}{2}=2\).

steps.stem: Three circles of radius 6 cm have centers A, B and C, with \(AB=BC=CA=6\) cm. What is the perimeter of their common region (in cm)?
explanation: Each side of triangle ABC is 6, the radius: the triangle is equilateral, and each angle is \(60°\).
The common region is bounded by three \(60°\) arcs. Each is \(\frac16\) of the circumference \(2\pi\cdot6=12\pi\): \(2\pi\).
Perimeter: \(3\cdot2\pi=6\pi\).

The outer ring: \(\pi(3c)^2-\pi(2b)^2=9\pi c^2-4\pi b^2\).

explanation: Angles ABD and ACD rest on the same arc AD, so \(\angle ACD=\angle ABD=\alpha\). Also \(\angle ADB=\alpha\).
\(\angle ADC=\angle ADB+\angle BDC=\alpha+24°\).
Triangle ACD: \(44°+\alpha+(\alpha+24°)=180°\), so \(2\alpha=112°\) and \(\alpha=56°\).

steps.stem: BD and EC are diameters of a circle with center O. A lies on the minor arc EB, and arcs EA and AB are equal. Given: angle ECA is \(3t\). What is angle DAC?
explanation: Angle ECA is an inscribed angle on arc EA, so the arc is \(2\cdot3t=6t\). Arc AB is equal: \(6t\).
Central angle EOB: \(6t+6t=12t\). The vertical angle DOC is also \(12t\).
Angle DAC is an inscribed angle on arc DC: \(\frac{12t}{2}=6t\).

steps.stem: Square ABCD is inscribed in a circle with circumference \(12\pi\) cm. E, F, G and H are the midpoints of its sides. What is the area of square EFGH (in cm²)?
explanation: Diameter: \(\frac{12\pi}{\pi}=12\). It is the diagonal of ABCD: area \(\frac{12^2}{2}=72\).
The square of the midpoints has half the area: \(\frac{72}{2}=36\).

steps.stem: A circle with center O has radius 4 cm. A and E lie on the circle, angle AOE is 45°, and B is the foot of the perpendicular from A to OE. What is the area of sector AOE outside triangle AOB (in cm²)?
explanation: The \(45°\) sector is \(\frac18\) of the disk: \(\frac18\cdot\pi\cdot4^2=2\pi\).
Triangle AOB is right and isosceles, with hypotenuse \(OA=4\): legs \(\frac4{\sqrt2}=2\sqrt2\), area \(\frac{2\sqrt2\cdot2\sqrt2}{2}=4\).
Sector outside the triangle: \(2\pi-4\).

steps.stem: Two concentric circles have radii 5 cm and 13 cm. A chord of the larger circle is tangent to the smaller circle. What is the chord’s length (in cm)?
explanation: The chord touches the small circle. The small radius to that point is perpendicular to the chord, so the distance from the center to the chord is 5.
This perpendicular cuts the chord in half: \(\sqrt{13^2-5^2}=\sqrt{144}=12\).
The chord: \(2\cdot12=24\).

steps.stem: In a circle with radius 5 cm, two parallel chords are 6 cm and 8 cm long. The center of the circle is between the two chords. What is the distance between the chords (in cm)?
explanation: Chord 8: half of it is 4, and its distance from the center is \(\sqrt{5^2-4^2}=3\).
Chord 6: half of it is 3, and its distance from the center is \(\sqrt{5^2-3^2}=4\).
The center is between the chords: \(3+4=7\). (1 is the distance when both chords are on the same side.)

steps.stem: In a circle with center O and radius 5 cm, chord AB is 8 cm long. Which of the following statements is true?
choices: The distance from O to AB is 4 cm
The area of triangle AOB is 12 cm²
explanation: The perpendicular from O cuts AB in half: 4 and 4. The distance: \(\sqrt{5^2-4^2}=3\), not 4.
Triangle AOB: \(\frac{8\cdot3}{2}=12\) — true.
If \(\angle AOB\) were \(90°\), AB would be \(5\sqrt2\approx7.07\), not 8. And \(\angle OAB=45°\) would need the distance (3) to equal the half chord (4).

steps.stem: The radius of a circle decreases by 10%. By what percent does its area decrease?
explanation: The radius is multiplied by 0.9, so the area is multiplied by \(0.9^2=0.81\).
The area is \(81\%\) of what it was: a decrease of \(100\%-81\%=19\%\).

steps.stem: The area between two concentric circles is \(45\pi\) cm². Their radii differ by 3 cm. What is the smaller radius (in cm)?
explanation: Difference of squares: \((R-r)(R+r)=45\). With \(R-r=3\): \(R+r=15\).
\(\begin{cases} R+r=15 \\ R-r=3 \end{cases}\) Subtract: \(2r=12\), so \(r=6\).

steps.stem: Two circles have the same center. A chord of the larger circle is 16 cm long and touches the smaller circle. What is the area between the two circles (in cm²)?
explanation: The small radius to the touching point is perpendicular to the chord and cuts it in half: \(h=8\).
Right triangle: \(R^2=r^2+8^2\), so \(R^2-r^2=64\).
Ring: \(\pi R^2-\pi r^2=\pi(R^2-r^2)=64\pi\) — we never needed R or r.

steps.stem: ABCD is a trapezoid with \(AD\parallel BC\), circumscribed about a circle with center O and radius 6 cm. The circle is tangent to CD at E and to BC at F. Given: angle ADC is 60°. What is the area of the minor sector EOF (in cm²)?
explanation: \(AD\parallel BC\), so the two angles on the leg CD add up to \(180°\): \(\angle BCD=180°-60°=120°\).
Radii to the points of tangency: \(OE\perp CD\) and \(OF\perp BC\). In quadrilateral OECF: \(\angle EOF=360°-90°-90°-120°=60°\).
Sector: \(\frac16\cdot\pi\cdot6^2=6\pi\).

\(\begin{cases} AB=6\text{ cm} \\ BC=10\text{ cm} \\ CD=14\text{ cm} \end{cases}\)
What is AD (in cm)?
explanation: Call the radii a, b, c and d. For tangent circles, the distance between the centers is the sum of the radii.
\(AB+CD=(a+b)+(c+d)\) and \(BC+AD=(b+c)+(a+d)\): both are the sum of all four radii.

A circle is inscribed in triangle ABC and touches side AB at D. Given:
\(\begin{cases} AB=10\text{ cm} \\ BC=12\text{ cm} \\ CA=8\text{ cm} \end{cases}\)
What is BD (in cm)?
explanation: Tangent pieces from one vertex are equal: x from A, y from B and z from C. \(\begin{cases} x+y=10 \\ y+z=12 \\ z+x=8 \end{cases}\)
Add the three equations: \(2(x+y+z)=30\), so \(x+y+z=15\).

steps.stem: Two externally tangent circles with centers A and B have radii 9 cm and 4 cm. A common tangent touches them at D and C, respectively. What is the perimeter of quadrilateral ABCD (in cm)?
explanation: Tangent circles: \(AB=9+4=13\). The radii AD and BC are perpendicular to the tangent DC, so ABCD is a right trapezoid.
Draw BE parallel to DC (E on AD): \(AE=9-4=5\) and \(BE=DC\).
Right triangle ABE: \(DC=\sqrt{13^2-5^2}=\sqrt{144}=12\).

steps.stem: Three circles of radius 2 cm are pairwise externally tangent. What is the area of the region between them enclosed by the three minor arcs joining their tangency points (in cm²)?
explanation: The centers form an equilateral triangle with side \(2+2=4\): area \(\frac{4^2\sqrt3}{4}=4\sqrt3\).
Inside the triangle, each circle has a \(60°\) sector. Three of them make \(180°\) — half of a disk with radius 2: \(\frac12\cdot\pi\cdot2^2=2\pi\).
The gap: \(4\sqrt3-2\pi\).

steps.stem: Two circles have radius 4 cm, and the distance between their centers is 4 cm. What is the area common to both disks (in cm²)?
explanation: Each center lies on the other circle: \(OA=OP=PA=4\) and \(OB=OP=PB=4\). Two equilateral triangles, so \(\angle AOB=120°\).
AB is twice the height of an equilateral triangle: \(AB=2\cdot2\sqrt3=4\sqrt3\). The distance from O to AB is \(\frac42=2\). Triangle AOB: \(\frac{4\sqrt3\cdot2}{2}=4\sqrt3\).
